summary: Point 22 backend-only verification. Tested create_or_activate_bill_incentive / sync_incentive_on_bill_status_change directly in Python (routes.staff._db = motor client) and admin incentive report (JSON + CSV) via public HTTP with admin JWT, using only throwaway P22TEST records (phones 7000022001/7000022002, brand doc 'P22TEST Brand' aliases ['P22TEST Alias']). No approve/reject/force-credit/reprocess/WhatsApp/OTP endpoints called. 16/16 pytest pass (4 existing + 12 new). All requested features work as specified. Extra probes found 2 robustness issues (concurrency race, duplicate no_active_attribution miss rows) - not in the stated acceptance criteria. Cleanup verified: 0 P22TEST/70000220xx rows left in retail_staff, staff_attributions, staff_incentives, staff_attribution_misses, bills, brands.

minor.issue: Race condition: the 'already' check (find_one on staff_incentives) and the attribution bind (update_one without a {used: False} condition) are not atomic, and there is no unique index on staff_incentives(type,bill_id). Probe: 3 concurrent evaluations of the same bill created 3 bill_upload incentive rows. 2 different bills evaluated at the same time against one scan produced 2 awards. This can happen with a double-clicked admin approve (BackgroundTask) or overlapping upload and approve paths, and it breaks the 'one eligible award per bill' rule.

A bill with no eligible attribution writes a new 'no_active_attribution' miss row on every re-evaluation (manual_review -> approved -> approved gave 3 rows for one bill). This is the same kind of duplicate that was already fixed for brand_mismatch, and it inflates reason_counts in the misses report. This behaviour predates this change.
If bill.created_at is missing, upload_at falls back to now(), so a QR scan made after the upload could be bound. 2 legacy TEST bills in Preview have created_at=None. Low risk.

action_items: Make awarding idempotent under concurrency: add a unique partial index on staff_incentives {bill_id:1,type:1} where type='bill_upload' (and catch DuplicateKeyError), and bind the scan atomically with find_one_and_update({id, used: False}, {$set: {used: True, used_by_bill_id}}) before inserting the award.
Dedupe no_active_attribution miss rows per bill_id (upsert keyed by bill_id + reason), as was done for brand_mismatch.
Optional: when bill.created_at is missing, skip binding (or use another upload timestamp) instead of falling back to now().
critical_code_review_comments: Non-atomic read-then-write in the award path (see minor issue 1). This is the main remaining risk to 'one award per bill'.

admin_incentive_report brand filter scans the whole brands and retail_staff collections on each request. Fine at the current scale; for larger data, consider caching or precomputing normalised brand keys.

Registration activation (14b) still uses strict normalised equality, not aliases. Per the request this is unchanged, but it differs from the alias-aware bill_upload match (e.g. a 'Domino's Pizza' bill would not activate a 'Dominos' registration unless the normalised strings are equal).

success_rate.backend: 100% (16/16 requested-scope tests); 2 extra robustness probes failed (concurrency, duplicate misses)
